portals.observation: The Ministry’s Swahili page names Arusha City among e-Ardhi councils. The platform requires an account for requests and application tracking. The public land-rent assessment page accepts title/plot IDs, owner type/name, area, block, and plot number; it is not a geometry-only service. No field was submitted and no account/login used. No anonymous parcel geometry was verified.

coverageAssessment.claimedScope: The official Ministry of Lands states that e-Ardhi was operational in Arusha City Council and describes it as providing land planning, surveying, title registration, and valuation services. The city council portal itself identifies Arusha City Council but does not expose a cadastral map or registry. This establishes city-specific service coverage, not public parcel geometry.
coverageAssessment.verifiedOpenScope: No anonymous public geometry-only parcel response was verified.

technicalBlocker: The city land-service platform is account-based; the public assessment workflow requires property/title and owner/location fields. No geometry-only anonymous service was identified.
